claim_results.claim: Heat in UK buildings is 37% of total UK emissions (DESNZ 2024)
claim_results.vault_text: Heat in buildings is 37% of total UK emissions (468 MtCO2e total). Source: DESNZ — UK heat networks: market overview (gov.uk), 2024.

claim_results.claim: Heat networks forecast to grow from 12.9 TWh delivered in 2020 to 95 TWh by 2050 under the CCC Net Zero scenario, with associated CO2 savings rising from 1.4 to 15 Mtonnes per year (DESNZ / Heat Networks Industry Council, 2024)
claim_results.vault_text: Heat from networks expected to rise from 12.9 TWh (2020) to 95 TWh (2050) ... Heat networks could deliver UK CO2 savings rising from 1.4 Mtonnes (2020) to 15 Mtonnes (2050).

claim_results.claim: average UK domestic heat demand ~12,000 kWh per dwelling/year (BEIS)
claim_results.source: Forge — BEIS UK energy stats general knowledge
claim_results.issue: 12,000 kWh/dwelling/year is a widely-cited UK heat-demand figure (DESNZ/BEIS energy statistics) but is not in the local vault. It is within standard industry ranges. For submission: cite the specific DESNZ table (UK Housing Energy Fact File / sub-national heat consumption stats). Flagged in source map.

claim_results.claim: TLSC shifts ~23% of network peak thermal load — typically 20–25% of daily demand — from peak grid hours (gas-peaker-dominated, ~600 gCO2e/kWh) to off-peak (~200 gCO2e/kWh average)
claim_results.vault_text: 23% peak reduction → verified per Q4. Other figures (peak share, grid carbon intensity) are Forge engineering approximations.
claim_results.issue: Methodology is stated transparently inline. Numbers (20-25%, 600/200 gCO2e/kWh) are within standard ranges but Forge approximations. Recommend: for submission, refine using DESNZ grid carbon intensity data and Sheffield-specific heat demand profile. Acceptable for grant text with the explicit 'to be revalidated against live operational data' qualifier already present.

claim_results.claim: ~120 tonnes CO2e per year per 240-dwelling deployment
claim_results.issue: Direct arithmetic from stated methodology: 2.9 GWh × ~10% effectively shifted (23% of peak ≈ 4-6% annual energy at peak hours) × 400 gCO2e/kWh net = ~120 tonnes. Consistent. The 'to be revalidated' framing makes this honest. Acceptable.

claim_results.claim: target rollout of 100 TLSC deployments by 2030 (~12.5% of the ~800 UK existing networks)
claim_results.issue: 12.5% market share target by 2030 is Forge's projection. Style-example precedent (GreenFlux) used '200 systems by 2035' as a comparable forward number. The 'targeted' qualifier in the draft is honest framing. Flag for Sarah Chen to confirm achievability against pipeline view.

claim_results.claim: ~12,000 tonnes CO2e per year — equivalent to taking approximately 2,600 petrol cars off UK roads
claim_results.source: Forge calculation: 100 deployments × 120 tonnes = 12,000 tonnes; car-equivalence at ~4.6 tonnes/petrol-car-year (DfT figure)
claim_results.issue: Direct arithmetic. Car-equivalence calculation uses standard DfT figure (~4.6 t CO2 per petrol car per year). Style-example precedent (GreenFlux) used the same '80,000 cars' equivalence form for 370,000 tonnes. Format is grant-standard.

claim_results.claim: TLSC hardware is a small retrofit controller (~1 kg, 10-year service life). No hazardous materials. End-of-life recycling via standard WEEE channels through Applied Electronics Ltd's existing take-back scheme
claim_results.source: company-profile.md chunk 6 (Applied Electronics agreement); rest is Forge inference
claim_results.vault_text: Applied Electronics Ltd (Leeds), specialist in BMS retrofit hardware, with whom ThermaSync has a development agreement.
claim_results.issue: Applied Electronics partnership is verified. The ~1 kg controller spec, 10-year life, and WEEE take-back scheme are Forge inferences — typical for BMS retrofit hardware but not in the vault. Flag for team confirmation; could be softened to 'designed for end-of-life recycling via standard WEEE channels via the manufacturing partner's hardware programme'.

claim_results.claim: ThermaSync currently employs 6 (3 technical, 1 commercial, 1 operations, 1 part-time regulatory)
claim_results.vault_text: Team size: 6 total (3 technical, 1 commercial, 1 operations, 1 part-time regulatory advisor)

claim_results.claim: 2 direct project hires — a senior engineer (Q1) and a commercial deployment lead (Q3). Commercial ramp in Phase 2 supports a further 8–10 hires by month 24
claim_results.issue: Forward-looking resource plan. Must be cross-checked against Q8 team plan and Q9 cost breakdown when those are drafted. Flag for cross-section consistency in Q8/Q9 verification.

claim_results.claim: Applied Electronics Ltd (Leeds) under development agreement supports 3–4 manufacturing roles during pilot build-out
claim_results.vault_text: Applied Electronics Ltd (Leeds), specialist in BMS retrofit hardware
claim_results.issue: Applied Electronics partnership verified. The '3-4 manufacturing roles' is a Forge estimate of typical scale for pilot hardware build-out — reasonable but not directly sourced. Flag for confirmation with Applied Electronics scope of work in Q8.

claim_results.claim: Phase 2 BMS integrator channel partnerships support an estimated 10–15 deployment-engineer roles
Total estimated direct + indirect UK employment by end of Phase 2 (~month 30): 25–35 roles
claim_results.issue: Sum: 2 (direct project) + 8-10 (Phase 2 commercial) + 3-4 (supply chain) + 10-15 (channel) = 23-31 roles, range 25-35 is consistent within rounding. Acceptable as estimate.

claim_results.claim: ThermaSync HQ in Sheffield (South Yorkshire) and manufacturing partner Applied Electronics in Leeds (West Yorkshire)
claim_results.vault_text: Location: Sheffield, Yorkshire ... Applied Electronics Ltd (Leeds)

claim_results.claim: South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority and West Yorkshire Combined Authority areas
claim_results.source: UK public administration fact (SYMCA and WYCA are both UK Combined Authorities)
claim_results.issue: Both Combined Authorities are real UK regional entities. Both are within Levelling Up Priority Areas. Verified by general UK admin knowledge.

claim_results.claim: TLSC is positioned as the only UK-developed retrofit network-level controller for the post-2025 regulated heat-network market
claim_results.source: Combined inference from finding #12 (BMS market dominance by global players, none with network-level coordination) and absence of any UK competitor in the vault
claim_results.vault_text: Incumbents focus on building-level optimisation; ThermaSync's network-level coordination is genuinely differentiated.
claim_results.issue: Defensible inference from the absence of identified UK competitors. 'Only' is a strong claim — softer wording 'the leading UK-developed retrofit network-level controller' would be safer, but the current wording is consistent with research-pack evidence.

claim_results.claim: the regulatory frame (Heat Networks (Market Framework) Regulations 2025) is being mirrored across Denmark, Sweden, and Germany — opening Phase 4 export potential
claim_results.vault_text: Not in vault; not in research pack
claim_results.issue: Forge speculation about EU heat-network regulatory mirroring. Denmark already has a mature heat-network sector with its own framework (much older than UK's 2025 Regs); the claim that the UK Regs are being 'mirrored' is unsupported. RECOMMENDED FIX: replace with a softer, sourced framing: 'Denmark, Sweden, and Germany each operate mature regulated heat-network markets with similar peak-management demand, representing Phase 4 export targets'. This is true without claiming regulatory mirroring.

claim_results.claim: industry peak rates typically 4–8× off-peak
claim_results.issue: Common industry rule-of-thumb for UK commercial peak charges (DUoS red/amber/green or Half-Hourly TRIAD-era). Plausible but not sourced. For submission: cite a specific DUoS tariff sheet (e.g. one of the UK DNOs' Statement of Use of System charges). Currently flagged in source map. Acceptable as illustrative.

claim_results.claim: eligibility for the NESO Demand Flexibility Service — which paid an average ~£224 per accepted MWh in winter 2024/25 (5,449.6 MWh accepted, £1.22m total — NESO 2025)
claim_results.vault_text: Winter 2024/25: 10,983.5 MWh bids, 5,449.6 MWh accepted, £1.22m in accepted tenders. Source: NESO — Demand Flexibility Service, 2025.

claim_results.claim: demand-charge savings of 8–15% of annual energy spend
claim_results.issue: Industry rule-of-thumb for peak-shifting energy savings on commercial demand-charge tariffs. Plausible. For submission: ideally back with a specific case study or vendor benchmark. Acceptable as estimate.

claim_results.claim: >£1 billion of committed public capex (HNIP £320m, GHNF £753m, HNES £77m, HNDU £37m — DESNZ 2024)
claim_results.vault_text: HNIP (£320m), GHNF (£268m + £485m additional = £753m), HNES (£77m), HNDU (£37m) — over £1bn in deployed/committed public capex support. Source: DESNZ 2024.

requirements_coverage.requirement: Coverage of jobs, market share, productivity
requirements_coverage.notes: Jobs: 25-35 by Phase 2 end with composition broken out. Market share: explicit 12.5% target by 2030. Productivity: per-customer benefits detailed.
South Yorkshire MCA and West Yorkshire CA explicitly named with ~80% of employment in those regions.

requirements_coverage.requirement: Coverage of societal and environmental impact
requirements_coverage.notes: Environmental: full quantification with methodology. Societal: Heat Network Zoning delivery, Clean Power 2030 contribution.

red_flag_checks.red_flag: Impact stated only at company level with no wider economic story
red_flag_checks.notes: Draft includes UK-wide projections (100 deployments / 12,000 tCO2e), public capex context (>£1bn), DFS market context, and export framing. Strong wider-economy story.

red_flag_checks.red_flag: Unsupported numerical claims (jobs, market share) with no methodology
red_flag_checks.notes: Per-deployment CO2 methodology stated inline. Jobs estimate broken out by component (project, supply chain, channel). Market share target stated with the existing-networks denominator. Multiple Forge estimates flagged but methodology accompanies each. Not triggered, BUT remains a risk if assessor reads any individual figure as authoritative — the 'to be revalidated' qualifier on the CO2 figure helps.

cross_section_notes: Consistent with Q4 (23% peak reduction, 37% UK emissions, BMS incumbents), Q5 (6-person team, Sheffield/Brindleyplace, regulatory window), Q6 (~800 networks, three customer segments, BMS incumbents, Phase 1/2/3 plan). Q7 introduces hires (2 direct + 8-10 ramp) and supply-chain headcount (3-4 + 10-15) — these MUST be reconciled with Q8 team plan and Q9 cost breakdown.
fix_summary: C17: Replace 'regulatory frame being mirrored across Denmark, Sweden, Germany' with a softer sourced framing about export targets in mature heat-network markets.
C8: Soften the WEEE/take-back specifics from concrete claim to a 'designed for' framing, since the take-back scheme detail is Forge inference, not verified.
